chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Safwan ibn Yahya from Hanan who said: I heard my father narrating from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Salman was sitting with a number of people from Quraish in the Masjid. They began tracing their lineage and elevating their ancestry until they reached Salman. Umar ibn al-Khattab said to him, 'Inform me, who are you, and who is your father, and what is your origin?' He said, 'I am Salman ibn Abdillah. I was astray, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, guided me through Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). I was needy, so Allah made me self-sufficient through Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). I was a slave, so Allah freed me through Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). This is my lineage, and this is my nobility.'

He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) came out, and Salman, may Allah be pleased with him, was speaking to them. Salman said to him, 'O Messenger of Allah, what did I encounter from these people? I sat with them, and they began tracing their lineage and elevating their ancestry until they reached me. Umar ibn al-Khattab said to me,

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O group of Quraish, indeed a man's nobility is his religion, and his chivalry is his character, and his origin is his intellect. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said:

Surely We have created you of a male and a female, and made you tribes and families that you may know each other; surely the most honorable of you with Allah is the one among you most careful (of his duty).

Then the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to Salman: 'None of these people has any superiority over you except by the fear of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and if piety is for you over them, then you are more preferable.'
ai.seo_question: What is the basis of true nobility in Islam according to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family)?
ai.summary: In this narrative from Al-Kafi, Salman al-Farsi counters the Quraysh's tribal elitism by defining his lineage through spiritual transformation—guidance, wealth, and emancipation via the Prophet—rather than bloodline. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) validates this by citing Surah Al-Hujurat 49:13, establishing that piety (Taqwa) and moral character (Akhlaq) supersede ancestral pride, a key concept in Shia theology regarding the merit of the faithful over tribal nobility.
